content:
After Mars Horizon 2 and some internal tooling, I joined the Warhammer Survivor team and release a demo to support our marketing beat. The demo have reached ~2700 concurrent players, and has driven thousands of wishlist per day.
Personal highlight for the demo is seeing some of the highest playtime for any game I have ever seen - and for a demo no less! It’s lovely to see how engaged the players are.
On the technical side, the demo was very stable with no significant bugs, which I am quite content with as well as I was getting very nervous on release thinking everything is going to blow up.
It is a surprisingly difficult project, turns out trying to display a ton of visual effects on low-end devices requires weird optimization, and working with 2 major IP holders there are often unexpected curveballs that we needed to dodge!
On top of the project itself, we also have to face 3 round of redundancies, a corporate acquisition and a change of studio director. The success of the title is a testament to the team’s resilience and dedication in a very challenging time.
Highlights:
Key programmer for demo releases. Liaise with QA and Design to create a successful and stable build. Creating tools for designer to analyze data and balance the game. Gameplay programming and bug squashing.
summary: Blending Warhammer with Vampire Survivors for a commercial success.
title: Warhammer Survivors

content:
After working for roughly 5-months for the Frogger Team in Q-Games, my quality of work is recognized and therefore transitioned into another team to help work on a project that was still under heavy development.
In the process, I worked with our animator to bring our main character to life in a 3D grid-based environment, implementing physics-related gameplay features, made tools for cinematic scene creation, and was in charge of most of the UIs for both the prototype and the final product. I am glad that the game was generally well received.
Highlights:
Cooperating with animators to create commercial-level animation for the main character. Implementing gameplay features that are vital to the core gameplay using maths and physics. Developing custom tools for Unity editor to assist debugging. Creating interactive UI for commercial purposes.
summary: 3D physics based puzzles with a frog, and you got a fairy following you around, how cute!
title: Frogger and the Rumbling Ruins

content:
For more about the state of the project please see here! Updating both site at the same time is a little bit too much for me currently. This is an experiment project primarily created for experiment, where I play with ideas such as custom editor tooling and try out new technology.
So far, I have built a few tools to help me build a game, some of which include:
Embedded scene editor for level editing Value Tracker that work innately with Unity’s profiler. Command Console Auto complete support Various custom inspector helper for easier animation editing (I have also made some pixelation shader and proper cel shading is on its way!) The project is for prototyping purposes and serves no commercial value. However it should serve a demo to my interest and ability.
summary: Personal play ground for a turn based tactic game.
title: Noneb Ni

content:
Please feel free to poke with the source code here. This is an experimental project I worked on to learn more about procedural generation and to play with another shiny new toy.
The project is for prototyping purposes and serves no commercial value. However, the possibility of creating a wide variety of trees using such a simple algorithm is fascinating to me.
I hence have a basic understanding of mesh manipulation and procedural generation.
Also, note that the algorithm was created by Nick and I held no credit for it. This work is done given Nick’s acknowledgment.
summary: Generating tree meshes on the fly, using a growth based model to make sure they always look organic.
title: Procedural Tree Generation

content:
This is an experimental project I worked on to learn some cutting-edge technologies and expose myself to various components of game development.
The primary purpose of the project is to explore the possibility of using Reinforcement Learning in game development. And more importantly, every programmer needs some new toys now and then :).
I also used this opportunity to try out some other things like procedural animation and 3D modeling.
Please feel free to poke with the source code here.
summary: Using reinforcement learning to build enemies for tower defense
title: Reinforcement Learning and Games

content:
During my time with Q-Games, I contributed to the continuous development of the famous franchise Frogger in Toy Town. Some of the more significant works include releasing a major update featuring a whole new game mode and the new “miniature” collectibles. The release was a huge success for the company as we see a spike in both retention rate and playtime.
In the process, I contributed by creating an interactive user interface that supports various input devices ranging from standard gamepads to the apple tv remote. I also assisted in other general bug fixes for gameplay.
My contribution is recognized and is therefore transitioned to another team to work on another work in progress project. In which I am responsible for both gameplay features and the UI.
Highlights:
Creating interactive UI that supports various input devices and has a heavy focus on UX. Experience in developing for Apple Arcade’s product in a double-A studio. Experience in localization to help the content reach a wider audience. Capable of supporting some of the “harder to deal with” languages such as Japanese and Arabic.
summary: Frog jump around on your apple devices. How charming.
title: Frogger in Toy Town

content:
During my time with Auroch Digital, I am the tool programmer for Mars Horizon 2. Whilst Mars Horizon 2 is still work in progress, the tools I created contributed heavily into the creation of our prototypes, and facilitated the release of the official trailer.
The announcement was a success, as we can observe in the Mars Horizon Discord, with many supporters of the prequel expressing their anticipation.
I am in charge of technical and feature design of most of our in-house tooling, from cinematic support for artists, data editor for designers, code generation for programmers and so on. In the process I am responsible from the very beginning, liaising with stakeholders, communicating timelines, to long term support and implementation.
I also pitched in for gameplay programming when the team need an extra pair of hand on deck.
Highlights:
Creating user-friendly UI that increase other team member’s productivity Code generation to improve productivity of programmers Extensive knowledge in tooling both in and outside of game engine
summary: A space exploration 4x game that doesn’t have guns.
title: Mars Horizon 2

content:
I was involved in the development of Cast(An In-Stadia display control software) in InCrowd Sports. Cast is a two-part software, with the highly customizable display control implemented using WPF and the rendering handled in Unity.
Due to the software nature, the solution we provide must be both reliable and highly customizable. The elegant solution we created sparked my interest in tools development. I am hence tainted with developing in WPF and am capable of using Unity outside of game development.
Highlights:
Interest and capability to create highly reliable and customizable tools to assist different workflows. Accustomed to working with best practices with a practical mindset.
summary: Turns out you can use Unity to control adverts in the stadia, really efficiently and dynamically as well.
title: In-Stadia Display Control

content:
I was involved in 18 different Android apps when I was working for InCrowd Sports. Some of the more significant work includes premium user authentication for videos in Crystal Palace FC and releasing Guinness PRO14.
The sheer amount of clients we were dealing with simultaneously and the new contracts the company is making introduced various challenges to maintaining a healthy code base and keeping up with the latest technology. I am proud to be part of the team that overcome these problems through joint effort across different disciplines.
I have hence developed strong UI programming skills and am reasonably familiar with Android development.
Highlights:
Creating a reliable and testable front end for commercial purposes Work across various codebase and create reusable libraries. Strong UI background and can provide insights from a mobile developer perspective. Also assisted in creating a continuous integration environment for other developers.
summary: I made all sort of sport apps, but none of them are about climbing, the only sports I can truly love.
title: Sport Mobile Apps

content:
Resume
I like cats, if we were to have a chat I will appreciate any cat gif you may have to hand.
I am Peter To. A tool programmer in UK working with Auroch Digital, Currently in charge of multiple in-house tooling within the studio and have directly worked on titles from traditional console to Apple Arcade.
Having worked in both games and non-games industries, I like to work with developers from various background, it’s often more efficient when the team comes from different part of the world - especially when you are trying to localize your game into 16 different languages.
Inspired by the GDC talk from Guerilla Games, I believe by empowering other team members to create content at their max capacity, my work will reach a wider audience and make a greater impact.
section: Hello! Welcome to my coding cave.
title: Hello! Welcome to my coding cave.

content:
I like working in games, but once upon a time I worked in enterprise software as well. From technical design to long term project maintenance, my experience spans across different platforms, like PC, mobile, to niche platform like Apple TV for Apple Arcade.
I specialize in tooling but well versed in gameplay and UI programming to wear the many different hats the indie scene demands. I also dabble in build pipeline to make sure my tools can build themselves.
In the past I have also worked on enterprise software and mobile apps, as all developers ought to do it at some point - it’s good for our health.
Feel free to let me know if you want to speak with someone about my performance - I can send you some emails to my references.
title: Work
